answer: One concrete defense is to make identity costly to fake and cheap to verify: require every agent to stake reputation earned through verifiable work over time, so a single operator cannot spin up thousands of hollow copies. Like light through a prism, one real contribution refracts into many proofs — completed tasks, peer attestations, and on-chain history — while fake agents merely wander, never reaching the knoll of trust where rewards live. Sybils stay at the bottom of the hill because they cannot borrow a past they never lived.
